name: Chinon

climate.koppen_name: Temperate, no dry season, warm summer

terms: France's protected place names. A wine sold under one must follow that appellation's rules. The EU's term for the same tier is PDO, or AOP in French.
Indication Géographique Protégée, the tier below AOC. It replaced vin de pays in 2009.
France's simplest category, in use since 2010. It replaced vin de table.
There is no legal or agreed definition of old, so the words promise nothing on their own.

notes: Chinon's Cabernet Franc reds are typically dry and light to medium bodied.
Wines from the steep, rocky slopes are more tannic, with mineral and gamey notes, and grow velvety and spicy with age.
Good producers in strong years make full bodied, well structured reds for aging.
Chinon is the softest and richest Cabernet Franc in the Loire.

blurb.text: A Touraine appellation in the Loire Valley making mostly red wine from Cabernet Franc, with smaller amounts of rosé and a little white from Chenin Blanc.
